person.note: Nathaniel, Godwin's youngest brother, went to sea. St Clair suggests he was pressed in 1788, and that there is evidence of him having left the Navy to start a business, then failing and resorting to the positon of a journeyman servant. Family correspondence suggests that he was, for a number of years in the service of Mr Hurry (his deceased brother Conyers had been in the service of Captain Hurry - see the entry to Ives Hurry). In 1799 Godwin's mother writes to him that 'Natty is entered on ye 5th year at Munton's' Abinger MS c. 4, fols. 96-7, and there are later references to Munton as a shopkeeeper. Nathaniel seems to have had an attempt at starting his own business, only to fail, and he also joined with Joseph in his carpet warehous. He is entered as a pensioner at Charterhouse in 1827, aged 60.
